newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adds Aruba to drug-transit country list.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adds Aruba to drug-transit country list.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday he has added the tiny Caribbean nation of Aruba to the U.S. list of major illicit drug-transit countries.
In a letter to Congress, Clinton also said the Netherlands Antilles in the Caribbean has been added to those countries Washington monitors as potentially significant drug-transit countries.
Problem drug-transit nations already include Cuba, Turkey, the Balkan route countries and the former poppy-growing countries of central Asia.

Regarding Aruba, Clinton told leaders of Congress that in the past two years smugglers have turned to Aruba for smuggling illegal drugs because of law enforcement crackdowns on other routes in the area.
"Taking advantage of the limited enforcement capabilities of most eastern Caribbean countries, Colombian drug syndicates have been routing U.S.-bound cocaine and heroin through the region," he said.
He said the vast majority of cocaine and heroin that transits Aruba is destined for the United States.
He also said an analysis of trafficking patterns indicates there is considerable drug activity taking place around the Netherlands Antilles, especially around St. Maarten.

The findings do not affect financial assistance to these countries. That happens in an annual survey when the United States announces whether a nation is certified for helping in the fight against drug trafficking.
If one is decertified, Washington acts to stem the flow of international assistance to that country.
